  • Pass a pre-employment medical along with Searson Buck Onboarding processes.

job.title: Inventory Coordinator
job.description:
Right Stock. Right Place. Right Time.

 We are partnering with a well-established Tasmanian business to recruit an experienced Inventory Coordinator. This is an excellent opportunity for a highly organised professional who enjoys the challenge of managing inventory, supplier relationships and purchasing activities while ensuring products are available when and where they're needed.

In this varied role, you will play a critical part in supporting operations across multiple branches in Tasmania by coordinating purchasing, maintaining stock accuracy, managing supplier performance and driving inventory optimisation initiatives. The position combines inventory management with internal stakeholder support to ensure operational efficiency and excellent customer outcomes.

Key Responsibilities
  • Raise and manage purchase orders with local and international suppliers.
  • Coordinate day-to-day inventory replenishment and bulk ordering requirements.
  • Monitor purchase orders, pricing, quantities and delivery timeframes.
  • Manage stock transfers between branches to support customer demand and reduce excess inventory.
  • Assist with forecasting and inventory planning for imported products.
  • Liaise with suppliers regarding production schedules, freight and delivery performance.
  • Drive excess and slow-moving stock reduction initiatives.
  • Monitor stock levels and maintain inventory data accuracy.
  • Follow up outstanding orders and communicate updated ETAs to stakeholders.
  • Maintain supplier records, freight information and inventory system data.
About You

To be successful, you will bring:
  • Previous experience in inventory control, purchasing, supply chain, warehouse coordination or stock management.
  • Strong organisational and time management skills.
  • High attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Excellent communication and relationship-building abilities.
  • A proactive approach to problem solving and continuous improvement.
  • Strong computer skills and confidence working with inventory management systems.
  • A customer-focused mindset and the ability to work collaboratively across multiple teams.
What's on Offer?
  • Diverse and engaging inventory and supply chain responsibilities.
  • Opportunity to make a genuine impact on business performance.
  • Supportive and collaborative team environment.
  • Stable, long-term career opportunity.
  • Ongoing training and development.
If you're passionate about inventory management and enjoy working in a fast-paced environment where no two days are the same, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Contracts Administrator
job.description:
Seeking an experienced Contracts Administrator to lead commercial performance across tendering, contract negotiation, project delivery and close-out.

This is a senior, hands-on role working closely with leadership, estimating, operations and project teams. The focus is on identifying risk early, protecting margin, improving commercial outcomes and ensuring contractual opportunities are captured.

You will bring strong commercial judgement and be comfortable working across tenders, contract negotiations, project forecasting, variations, claims and complex commercial issues.
Key responsibilities
  • Lead commercial and contractual reviews of tenders and major opportunities.
  • Review and negotiate client, supplier and subcontractor contracts.
  • Identify and manage contractual and commercial risk.
  • Provide commercial input into pricing, margins and risk allowances.
  • Monitor project margins, forecasts, cost-to-complete and cash flow.
  • Oversee claims, variations, extensions of time and contractual notices.
  • Manage significant commercial negotiations and disputes.
  • Support Project Managers with practical commercial and contractual advice.
  • Oversee key supplier and subcontractor commercial arrangements.
  • Strengthen commercial processes, reporting and controls.
  • Develop commercial capability across project and operational teams.
About you You will be an experienced commercial professional with:
  • Commercial management, contracts or quantity surveying experience within construction, engineering, infrastructure, utilities or industrial services.
  • Strong knowledge of contract formation, administration, claims and variations.
  • Experience reviewing and negotiating complex contracts.
  • Working knowledge of the AS 4000 suite and Australian contracting frameworks.
  • Strong understanding of project margins, forecasting, cost-to-complete and cash flow.
  • Experience managing variations, claims and contractual disputes.
  • Strong negotiation and stakeholder management skills.
  • The ability to identify commercial risk and turn it into practical action.
  • Confidence working with senior management and operational teams.
A relevant qualification in quantity surveying, construction management, engineering, commerce, business or law would be highly regarded.

job.title: Project Manager
job.description:
Project Manager | Major Commercial Construction Project | Tasmania Lead the Delivery of a Landmark Commercial Construction Project | FIFO option available

An exceptional opportunity exists for an experienced Project Manager to join a nationally recognised commercial builder delivering a major construction project in Tasmania.

This is a career-defining opportunity to take ownership of a large-scale commercial development, leading project delivery from construction through to completion while managing client relationships, commercial performance, program outcomes, and multidisciplinary project teams. The Project Manager is responsible for overall project delivery, head contract obligations, commercial performance, design coordination, and leadership of site, engineering, and commercial teams.

Based in Devonport or Launceston, Tasmania you will join a high-performing leadership team delivering one of Tasmania's most significant commercial construction projects.

The Opportunity Reporting to the Project Director, you will be responsible for the successful delivery of a major commercial construction project, ensuring safety, quality, programme, and financial objectives are achieved. The role requires an experienced construction professional who can confidently lead project teams, manage client expectations, oversee contract administration, and drive project performance from start to finish.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead the overall delivery of a major commercial construction project.
  • Manage head contract obligations, contractual correspondence, and client communications.
  • Oversee project budgets, forecasts, variations, claims, and commercial performance.
  • Manage extension of time (EOT) submissions and contract compliance requirements.
  • Coordinate site, engineering, design, and commercial teams to achieve programme milestones.
  • Lead project meetings and stakeholder engagement activities.
  • Drive project safety, quality, and operational outcomes.
  • Provide leadership and direction to Site Managers, Engineers, Contract Administrators, and project teams.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, consultants, and subcontractors. 
About You To be successful, you will ideally possess:
  • 10+ years' experience in commercial construction project management.
  • Proven experience delivering major commercial building projects valued at $150M+.
  • Strong knowledge of head contract administration, variations, claims, and EOT management.
  • Experience managing large multidisciplinary project teams.
  • Excellent commercial acumen and stakeholder management skills.
  • Tertiary qualifications in Construction Management, Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • Experience within Tier 1, Tier 2, or leading commercial construction contractors highly regarded.
What's On Offer
  • FIFO arrangements may be considered for the right candidate with proven experience delivering major commercial construction projects.
  • Opportunity to lead a landmark commercial construction project in Tasmania.
  • Long-term career progression with a nationally recognised contractor.
  • Competitive salary package and executive-level career opportunity.
  • Strong project pipeline and future opportunities beyond the current project.
  • Collaborative and high-performing leadership team.
  • Devonport or Launceston location.
Why Apply? If you have a track record of successfully delivering large-scale commercial construction projects and are looking for an opportunity to leave a lasting impact on Tasmania's built environment, this role offers the scale, challenge, and career progression to take your career to the next level.

job.title: Pub Banc Group - RRSI & Career Connector Support Registration
job.description:
Pub Banc Group Impacted Employee - Rapid Response Skills Initiative (RRSI) & Career Connector Registration 
 
Register here for Career Connector support to access the Rapid Response Skills Initiative (RRSI) that provides up to $3,000 of funding for Training for employees impacted by business closure, downsizing or retrenchment. 

Funded by the Tasmanian Government, Jobs Tasmania.

That training could be for Re-skilling, Work Related Tickets and Certifications to support and enhance the employability of workers that have been made redundant within the last 12 months. 

The Career Connector service will connect you to personalised Career Support to improve your employability with access to RRSI funded training and a Free Jobs Matching Service.  Career Connector provides advice with Training, connects you to the Network of Regional Local Jobs Hubs, relevant Service Providers and supports you into Employment Opportunities to re-establish your career. 
 
To be eligible, you must meet all of the below criteria: 
  • have lost Casual, Full-time or Part-time work in the last 12 months due to Business Closure, Business Downsizing or Retrenchment
  • be an Australian Citizen or Permanent Resident with a Tasmanian Residential address
  • provide written evidence of job loss, redundancy or retrenchment (a Separation Certificate indicating Redundancy or Email/ Written Evidence of Redundancy)
  • If you were employed by Local, State or Australian Government or Government Department, Business or Government Enterprise, you may not be eligible for RRSI funded training.
For more information contact:

Justin at Career Connector

cc@searsonbuck.com.au

  • have lost Casual, Full-time or Part-time work in the last 12 months due to Business Closure, Business Downsizing or Retrenchment
  • be an Australian Citizen or Permanent Resident with a Tasmanian Residential address
  • provide written evidence of job loss, redundancy or retrenchment (a Separation Certificate indicating Redundancy or Email/ Written Evidence of Redundancy)
  • If you were employed by Local, State or Australian Government or Government Department, Business or Government Enterprise, you may not be eligible for RRSI funded training.
